newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia details rates to replace state taxes.
newsitem.headline: Australia details rates to replace state taxes.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Wednesday announced new levels of national taxes on tobacco, alcohol and petrol to replace state excises declared illegal by the country's highest court.
Costello said the national government's customs and excise duty on petrol would increase by 8.1 cents a litre and on tobacco by A$167 a kg.
The wholesale tax on alcohol will increase by 15 percentage points, he said in a statement.

Costello said earlier on Wednesday his government would replace state and territory taxes rendered invalid by a High Court ruling on Tuesday, and return the money to Australia's six states and two territories.
The court ruled the states and territories did not have the constitutional power to levy the excises -- a decision that outlawed A$5 billion, or 16 percent, of their income.

"In response to a unanimous request from the states and territories, the Commonwealth (national government) has agreed to introduce measures to protect state and territory revenue following yesterday's High Court decision," Costello said.

The new taxes will be uniform across all states and territories. Those that previously had lower rates will have to refund the difference to manufacturers or wholesalers to prevent price rises. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
